name: Acute Undifferentiated Leukemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of ≥20% blasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Absence of definitive myeloid, B-cell, or T-cell lineage markers by immunophenotyping
Blasts with undifferentiated morphology lacking lineage-specific cytochemical staining
Absence of recurrent genetic abnormalities defining other acute leukemias

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: ≥20% blasts in marrow or blood with absence of lineage-specific markers and undifferentiated blast morphology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other acute leukemias by immunophenotyping and genetic studies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Undifferentiated blast proliferation in bone marrow
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic immature blast cells lacking lineage markers
searchTerms: excess immature blood cells in marrow
abnormal immature cell growth in bone marrow
low blood cell counts from marrow failure
reduced red, white, and platelet cells
pancytopenia due to bone marrow problems
pale skin and tiredness from anemia
fatigue and pallor due to low red blood cells
recurrent infections due to immune weakness
infections caused by low white blood cells

common.symptomName: Petechiae and mucosal bleeding from thrombocytopenia
searchTerms: small red spots and bleeding from low platelets
temperature rise with no infection found
losing weight and sweating at night

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with neurological deficits
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to CNS involvement
tumor of immature white blood cells
lung problems from blood cell buildup

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing ≥20% undifferentiated blasts
Bone marrow biopsy with hypercellularity and blast predominance
Cytochemical stains negative for myeloperoxidase and nonspecific esterase
imaging: Chest X-ray may show infiltrates if leukostasis present
Ultrasound or CT may reveal hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy
other: Immunophenotyping showing blasts negative for myeloid (CD13, CD33), B-cell (CD19, CD20), and T-cell (CD3) markers

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of myeloid lineage markers and myeloperoxidase positivity
Specific genetic abnormalities such as t(8;21), inv(16)
Expression of B-cell or T-cell lineage markers
Co-expression of myeloid and lymphoid markers
Distinct immunophenotypic profile differentiating from undifferentiated blasts

references: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 5th Edition, 2017
Arber DA et al. Acute undifferentiated leukemia: diagnostic criteria and clinical features. Blood. 2016.
